@constructor-igor Do you feel like fixing this one? My guess is that parameterized tests, which are suites, are not being handled correctly with respect to this Attribute. What should be happening is that the default timeout in the TestExecutionContext gets updated by the suite initialization and then used by each method. My guess is that no initialization is happening, since this is not a fixture. You can see how it should work by tracing through execution of a test fixture with Timeout attribute on it.

The cancelled tests would suggest that _some_ of what should be happening is happening, but on the wrong level. TimedOut tests are cancelled but we should actually recognize why they were cancelled and report them as failures, not timeouts.
@CharliePoole I'll try to check and suggest a fix in a few days. if not, I'll inform you.
Great. Be sure to include missing test cases in our tests.
